critical_code_review_comments: backend/routes/dev_os_builders.py — CLEAN: 59 lines, single responsibility, correct workspace scoping via _get_project, proper 400 on unknown builder key, audit log written on every PUT. No issues.

BuildersHub.jsx (419 lines) — well-organised with per-builder Editor components and static compose functions; still within the 700-line soft cap. Nit: multiple cards in a builder produce duplicate data-testids (e.g. two Logic cards both render bh-rule-when + bh-rule-then). This is why my test had to use locator().nth(i) with .input_value() to disambiguate. Consider suffixing with card index: `bh-rule-when-${i}` / `bh-rule-then-${i}` etc. for testability across the workflow/data/form editors too (bh-data-name, bh-role-name, bh-flow-trigger, bh-form-name, bh-report-measure, bh-int-what all suffer the same duplication when multiple items exist).

BuildersHub.jsx line 313 — builder.compose(spec) runs on every render synchronously; for very large specs this is fine, but consider useMemo keyed on active+spec to avoid recompute when only 'dirty' state changes.

BuildersHub.jsx line 291 — `const spec = specs?.[active] || builder.empty();` — because empty() returns a fresh object each render, the initial 'add item' click compares stale identity. Not a correctness bug (state ends up correct because setSpec merges by key) but could cause an eslint react-hooks/exhaustive-deps warning if the object were ever passed to a memoized child.

BuildersHub.jsx onBuild callback returns before the /talk request completes; the toast 'Sent to @devmanager — watch the chat' fires optimistically. If /talk 4xx/5xx, the toast is a lie. Consider awaiting the parent submit or wiring an error path through onBuild.
BuildersHub.jsx save-draft errors show generic 'Couldn't save the spec' — no HTTP status distinction (e.g., 401 auth loss vs 500). Low priority.

Backend PUT /builders/{key} does NOT run Pydantic validation on the SHAPE of each spec (all fields are Dict[str,Any]); a malicious client could store arbitrary blobs under builder_specs.data. If the shape ever informs @devmanager prompt directly, this is a small prompt-injection surface. Consider a per-key Pydantic model or at minimum a top-level schema/limit on nesting depth + max serialized size.

No rate-limit on PUT /builders/{key} — a runaway UI could spam saves on every keystroke. The current UI only saves on button click, but adding a lightweight per-user rate limit (e.g., 20/min) would be defensive.
